what: Which of the darkroom's 68 plates can be authored as engine positives today, and what blocks the rest. Measured from the registry GLSL.
corrected: An earlier version of this file said twelve plates were blocked on a missing stateful-loop construct. That was WRONG: `s.orbit` already is that construct - static bound, runtime break off a lever, named fields carried across iterations, and every update computed into a temporary before any field is assigned back, which is the correctness requirement such a loop has. `collatz` has been using it to emulate uint arithmetic in exact small floats since before this file existed. The claim was made from reading emit.mjs's `sum` and `descend` and not looking further. Ten of the fourteen are portable today; four are not.

the_vocabulary_that_exists.sum(n, k => term): a bounded float reduction, no carried state.
the_vocabulary_that_exists.descend(grid2(...), levels, {child, keep: a hierarchical subdivision walk with a fixed body shape.
the_vocabulary_that_exists.s.orbit(n, init, (st, k) => ({...}), {un: THE stateful bounded loop. Carries named float fields; a vec2 rides as two fields and a uint hash as exact small floats, which is what collatz does. Returns the fields plus `count` and `escaped`.

portable_today.note: throughput is 36,291 chars and vlsi 25,450 - long ports rather than blocked ones. None of these ten currently splits across the three cards, so porting them is robustness rather than a fix.

blocked.the_actual_blocker: orbit's step arrow must BE an object literal - `(st, k) => ({ ... })`. emit.mjs refuses any other body outright. So the step cannot declare an intermediate, and cannot contain a nested sum() or a nested orbit. These four have loops nested two and three deep: cascade advects a parcel through a per-step sum over octaves; rule30, rulespace and universal step a cellular automaton row.
blocked.the_change_that_unlocks_them: allow the step arrow a BLOCK body - local `const` declarations followed by a returned object literal - so a nested sum() or orbit can be declared inside it. The emitter already emits statements into the enclosing indent, and orbit already sequences its writeback correctly, so this is a parser and body-shape change rather than a new loop.
blocked.priority: cascade is the one that matters: it is the only plate that both still splits across the three cards and has no positive. Every other splitter either has a positive already or was fixed by getting one.

how_this_was_measured: darkroom/spec.py load_plates(), then per plate: count for-loops inside shape_*, and track brace depth to find the deepest nesting. Nesting >= 2 is the blocked set.

vocabulary_gaps_found_by_the_sweep.how_these_were_found: Not by design review. Each was hit by an agent converting a plate, reported rather than worked around, and in two cases hit independently by three agents before anyone wrote it down.

two_independent_causes: its `span` wants the cell count as an INT, and the emitter refuses a lever whose step is not 1 - `lever cells used where an integer is required, but it is not an integer lever` (CELLS has step 32)
the window result exposes only seat(); `const lo = w.win;` fails with `cannot bind lo: unhandled value`, and these plates read win.x/y/z/w in up to five places
s.window is unreachable for the sheet pl.what_the_agents_did: wrote the sheet lattice in floats instead, and measured the cost rather than waving at it. rule30 enumerated all 30,096 lever settings with f32 rounding: the visible row and cell ranges are IDENTICAL to the plate's integer window at every one, bounds differing by at most 8/1024 of a cell and never crossing an edge. universal enumerated its 8,208 settings: 15 of 16,416 window components differ, always by exactly one lattice unit, all at the single corner where the plate's own arithmetic exceeds f32's exact-integer range.
s.window is unreachable for the sheet pl.verdict: not blocking, measured, and worth closing anyway - three plates paying the same tax is a vocabulary problem rather than three plate problems

no float to int conversion.detail: Math.trunc is in the subset only as trunc(int/int); s.pick and s.depth take a literal or a lever, never a runtime bound. So `tl = rlo + int(u * (rhi - rlo + 1))` cannot be an int at all.
no float to int conversion.consequence: a runtime-computed index cannot address anything the vocabulary indexes by int, which is why universal could not have fed seat() even if win were readable

no uint, no bitwise operators, no hashu.detail: Ten of the thirteen conversions re-keyed an addressed hash chain through s.vnoise at whole lattice coordinates. That restates the law and draws a different member of the same ensemble, which the CONVERSION.md rule now explicitly permits.
no uint, no bitwise operators, no hashu.the_one_case_it_costs_something: throughput reads overlapping BITFIELDS of one word rather than successive draws off a chain, so the substitution changes the arrangement visibly - an 18x27 core where the shader lays out 20x24. It names the exact construct that would close it: a uint-typed expression in the subset, hashu over an int expression plus ^ & | >> << % and u2f. NOT a re-seedable sub-stream.
no uint, no bitwise operators, no hashu.verdict: the largest single gap in the vocabulary, and the only one that has changed a picture rather than only a hash
